reason: VALUE. (1) The claim that premise (4) is 'falsified for end-anchored nodes' goes further than the evidence. Probe 50 changed two knobs at once (ILP 0.4 + READMIT 0.94). round24/scan_recheck.json (R24-NF) already found that its '+' cannot be split between them: forks +4 = +3 safe divisions from ILP 0.4 + 1 insertion from READMIT, and nodes +1,076, of which +1,022 come from READMIT. exp85b and exp85c were never scored (none in RESULTS.md). The +0.002 can be explained entirely by the division channel (score = adj_edge + 0.1*div_J), and then READMIT's extra nodes are <= break-even, exactly as premise (4) says. JT's +0.001 per knob is from his fork and only a weak prior for our base. (2) The only direct measurement of the proposed step goes against it. In the dummy-clip GT lab (scratchpad r26/dummy_lab_summary.json), exp86c has IDENTICAL TP/FP/FN to exp85a (2049/99/78) and scores 0.921747 vs 0.921842: 44b6 and 6bba are both lower. The 388 extra READMIT 0.92 nodes gain 0 edge TPs and pay only the node-count factor J*(1-0.1*dN/N). The 11:17Z gate also shows forks 84 vs 85: RA92 moves one clip-4 safe division out, which touches the one channel that plausibly produced probe 50's gain. The lab is noise-level, but it is the only data, and it is <= 0. (3) Even the revived byteext prior was centred at +0.0007, below display resolution. P(display >= 0.959) ~0.2-0.25 is roughly what a ~0-effect change gets from rounding and noise on a single embryo. Selecting on that flip is public fitting, and its private (~71%) EV is ~0 to slightly negative. (4) The 'inconsistency' argument does not hold. DIS 2.25 was kept because its direction comes from the metric formula, not from a read. RA92 was excluded because it extends a threshold along a public-read direction. That difference is the user's stated criterion, not an oversight. FEASIBILITY: exp86c is built with a dummy PASS (WAIVER) and 0 GPU, and the M2 non-CI slot by 11:30 UTC is reachable, so it is technically fine. But (a) the user confirmed the night and morning at 12:25Z as 'stack of the night winners', after the 12:23Z exclusion of READMIT 0.92. (b) Round 26's own scan_plancheck and scan_hyp_morning already log 'READMIT 0.92/0.90 stay excluded / not re-proposed'. (c) exp86c sits on exp85a with no SEC. If exp89p (K + SEC) reads '+', exp86c is off the current-best base, against the 'arms off the current best' principle, and the SEC + RA92 variant is not built. (d) The trigger 'DIS reads 0/-/?' has no mechanism link to RA92: a flat DIS read says nothing about whether extra end-anchored nodes pay. Spending the last non-CI slot on a ~0-EV public-direction step displaces a stack of the night winners.
